prompt: An online store shows ad version 1 to a random sample of $100$ visitors and ad version 2 to another random sample of $100$. Version 1 gets $60$ clicks; version 2 gets $45$. For the test of $H_0: p_1 = p_2$, use the pooled proportion $\hat{p}_c = \frac{60 + 45}{200}$ and the formula $z = \frac{\hat{p}_1 - \hat{p}_2}{\sqrt{\hat{p}_c(1-\hat{p}_c)\left(\frac{1}{n_1} + \frac{1}{n_2}\right)}}$. What is $z$? Round to two decimal places.
explanation: $z = 0.15/0.0706 \approx 2.12$. The two-sided $p$-value is about $0.034$, so at $\alpha = 0.05$ there is convincing evidence the click rates differ.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why pool?
steps: $H_0$ says both ads have the SAME click rate. Our best single estimate of that common rate uses all 200 visitors: $105/200 = 0.525$.
Using one shared $\hat{p}_c$ in the standard error keeps the test consistent with what it assumes.
